claim_1.statement: Certified nested Sinkhorn does deliver a VALID two-sided bound at the root on the tiny common-model targets.
claim_1.test: L <= exact_dp <= U checked at every epsilon on all 20 tiny instances (5 fixtures x k in {1,2} x 2 cost families); 120 level checks.
claim_1.result: held everywhere; max dual-feasibility violation before the verification shift 3.25e-16, max repaired-plan marginal residual 1.11e-16

claim_2.statement: It does NOT reach the 1e-9 match to exact_dp on the only non-degenerate tiny fixture, and the obstruction is a measured cost law, not an implementation defect.
claim_2.test: epsilon schedule 5e-2..1e-4; root interval width and iterations recorded per level; iterations-to-tolerance measured on the costliest local subproblem at 3 epsilon levels.
claim_2.result: width = Theta(epsilon) (1.264e-2 at 5e-2 -> 1.791e-5 at 1e-4) while iterations = Theta(1/epsilon) (iterations*epsilon = 25.0, constant within 1%); work for width w is Theta(1/w), so w=1e-9 extrapolates to 2.5e10 iterations (~2.8e6 s at the measured 9.05e3 it/s) on ONE 2x2 subproblem

claim_3.statement: The same comparator meets the objective's 0.005 relative root gap cheaply, so it is eligible for the certified-quality track but not for the exact track.
claim_3.result: 0.005 relative root gap first met at epsilon=5e-2 or 1e-2 on all 14 instances with a positive root value; undefined for the 6 instances whose true value is 0

proposal: Score nested Sinkhorn only on the certified-quality track (valid root interval width at fixed total compute), never on the exact/1e-9 track.
Any exact-track competitor must be compared against exact backward induction, not against this comparator.

Preregister the relative-gap convention for zero-value instances BEFORE the grid: a positive-width interval can never meet a relative threshold when V=0, so those cells need an absolute criterion or must be excluded by declaration.

Do not adopt any no-progress/stagnation stopping heuristic for Sinkhorn on this target: the marginal residual plateaus for Theta(1/epsilon) iterations before dropping, so such a rule silently returns unconverged plans and inflates the certified upper bound (observed: root upper stuck at 0.5625 vs true 0.5).
not_claimed: coverage of T=50 or the required delta grid
